intro: Look up at Sillyon, an ancient city in Antalya province, from the 5th century BC. It stands on a flat-topped hill over the plain. This was one of the few Anatolian cities Alexander failed to take, and the longest known inscription in the Pamphylian dialect was found here.
history: Picture a flat-topped hill with sheer sides rising above the plain. On it stood one of the four great cities of Pamphylia. In 333 BC Alexander besieged it and withdrew without taking it — one of the few places in Anatolia to end that way. Its Hellenistic tower and gate system largely survive. The hill itself proved less lasting: in 1969 a landslip carried away part of it, and the theatre and stadium with it.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Hellenistic tower, the main gate and its ramp, the cisterns and the Seljuk-period buildings.
facts: Did you know? The inscription found here is the longest known text in the Pamphylian dialect, a branch of Greek recorded nowhere else. And when Alexander besieged the city in 333 BC, he withdrew without taking it — one of the few places in Anatolia to end that way.
outro: This brings our tour of Sillyon to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
